key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on component chemistry and addition order: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide helps passivate the surface.
engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor composition and mixing sequence could help preserve MXenes during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Exposed MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Used X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track chemical and surface changes.
Applied density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS analysis and DFT calculations support rapid degradation by iodine/polyiodides, slower PbI2-induced oxidation, and hydrogen-bond-mediated passivation by MAI.
watch_item: Results concern a model MAPbI3 precursor environment; the abstract reports no device-efficiency or operational-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
